headline: 6 madrasas in 16 days: Child sexual abuse allegations spark outrage across Bangladesh
summary: Reports of rape and abuse of children as young as seven in Gazipur, Savar, Dhaka, Kushtia and Pabna have led to protests and arrests.
details: Allegations of rape, attempted rape, and sexual abuse of children at six different madrasas across Bangladesh have emerged in just 16 days, sparking widespread public outrage.
In Gazipur, a 23-year-old teacher was arrested for allegedly raping an eight-year-old residential student on three consecutive nights, threatening the child into silence.
In Tongi, a teacher was detained after allegedly sexually abusing a seven-year-old girl. The incident led to locals assaulting the accused and vandalising the institution.
In Savar, a madrasa owner and headteacher allegedly raped a 13-year-old student, while his wife was arrested for allegedly aiding the crime and threatening the victim.
In Pabna and Kushtia, multiple teachers were arrested following allegations of attempted rape and sexual abuse of residential students, leading to further vandalism and arson.
Rights groups have warned that protests alone cannot ensure safety, calling for stronger monitoring and the establishment of anti-sexual harassment panels at every institution.
Religious Affairs Minister Kazi Shah Mofazzal Hossain Kaikobad described the abuse as 'extremely distressing and shameful,' pledging that the government will take necessary preventive measures.
Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh has called for fair investigations and exemplary punishment for the abusers, while condemning mob justice and vandalism of the institutions.
caption:
Six madrasas, 16 days, children as young as seven. The scale of alleged child sexual abuse is sparking outrage across the country.

Allegations of rape, attempted rape, and sexual abuse of children at six different madrasas across Bangladesh have emerged in just 16 days, sparking widespread public outrage.

In Gazipur, a 23-year-old teacher was arrested for allegedly raping an eight-year-old residential student on three consecutive nights, threatening the child into silence.

In Tongi, a teacher was detained after allegedly sexually abusing a seven-year-old girl. The incident led to locals assaulting the accused and vandalising the institution.

In Savar, a madrasa owner and headteacher allegedly raped a 13-year-old student, while his wife was arrested for allegedly aiding the crime and threatening the victim.

In Pabna and Kushtia, multiple teachers were arrested following allegations of attempted rape and sexual abuse of residential students, leading to further vandalism and arson.

Rights groups have warned that protests alone cannot ensure safety, calling for stronger monitoring and the establishment of anti-sexual harassment panels at every institution.

Religious Affairs Minister Kazi Shah Mofazzal Hossain Kaikobad described the abuse as 'extremely distressing and shameful,' pledging that the government will take necessary preventive measures.

Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh has called for fair investigations and exemplary punishment for the abusers, while condemning mob justice and vandalism of the institutions.

headline_marked: Japan eyes [[$6.35 billion private investment]] in Bangladesh, including car plants
headline: Japan eyes $6.35 billion private investment in Bangladesh, including car plants
summary: Japanese firms may start assembling and manufacturing vehicles locally, with Toyota planning a hybrid electric plant and service centers.
details: Japan is exploring approximately $6.35 billion in private-sector investment in Bangladesh over the next five years, focusing on the automotive, energy, and manufacturing sectors.

Japanese companies, including Toyota, Honda, and Nissan, may shift from exporting to manufacturing cars and parts locally. This move aligns with Tokyo's 'China Plus One' policy to diversify industrial ties.
Toyota Tsusho Corporation plans to invest $40 million in sales, service, and spare-parts centers in Dhaka and Chattogram by November 2026.
Additionally, Toyota is planning a hybrid electric vehicle manufacturing facility in the National Special Economic Zone, with development starting in 2027 and full production targeted for 2029.

Kazuiki Kataoka of JETRO noted that Bangladesh must first assemble vehicles from imported parts and then build local capacity in steel, chemicals, and precision engineering for full-scale manufacturing.
Beyond autos, energy infrastructure presents a major opportunity. JERA, Japan's largest power generator, is interested in expanding energy supply and LNG-related businesses.
The Matarbari deep-sea port in Cox's Bazar, developed with JICA support, is also seen as a key avenue for future Japanese investment.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will visit Japan from October 26 to 29, where he will meet Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae to advance these strategic and economic ties.

Kazuiki Kataoka of JETRO noted that Bangladesh must first assemble vehicles from imported parts and then build local capacity in steel, chemicals, and precision engineering for full-scale manufacturing.
